topics.title: Krispy Kreme Got Into 2,400 McDonald's. Then Krispy Kreme Quit

demand.title: Krispy Kreme Is (Finally) Getting What They Deserve...

topics.hook: Krispy Kreme got its doughnuts into McDonald's, and Krispy Kreme is the one that walked away.
topics.angle: A glazed doughnut in a McDonald's bag. March 2024: the two announce Krispy Kreme in every U.S. McDonald's by the end of 2026. By spring 2025 it is in about 2,400 of about 13,500. July 2, 2025: it ends, because Krispy Kreme could not bring its costs in line with how many doughnuts sold (its own filing); its shares had fallen more than 73% that year. Payoff: 2,400 of 13,500. Global beat: Krispy Kreme is in 40+ countries and says it will grow abroad instead.

topics.title: Toyota Built 450 Prototypes Before Anyone Heard of Lexus

demand.title: Toyota Spent $1 Billion to Beat Mercedes

topics.hook: Toyota built four hundred and fifty prototypes of one car, because its best customers kept leaving for Mercedes.
topics.angle: A Lexus badge on a car in a parking lot. 1984: Toyota starts a secret flagship project because customers who could afford more left for Mercedes or BMW (Toyota's own history). About six years, about 450 prototypes, more than 3.5 million km of testing, about $1 billion. September 1989: Lexus opens in the U.S. at $35,000; by the end of 1989 it hits its 16,000-car forecast. Payoff: 450 prototypes (or the $1 billion). Our angle is the prototypes and the leaving customers, not Rise Fall Repeat's $1 billion title.

topics.title: Kodak Sold a Camera for $1. Then It Invented the One That Ended It

demand.title: How Kodak Turned a $1 Camera Into a Fortune

topics.hook: Kodak put a camera in every hand for one dollar, and then built the camera that took them all away.
topics.angle: The thing in your hand: a camera, and the film you paid for every roll. 1900: the Brownie sells for $1, film 15 cents a roll (Kodak's own milestones), so Kodak earns on every picture you take. 1975: a Kodak engineer, Steve Sasson, builds the first digital camera, the size of a toaster, 10,000 pixels. No film, so nothing to sell after the camera. 1988: 145,300 people work for Kodak. January 2012: Chapter 11, 18,800 left (AP). Payoff: 145,300 to 18,800. Global beat: the filing left Kodak's international operations out (AP).
topics.why_now: A camera and a roll of film the viewer's family held; a settled story told from Kodak's own milestones page and the AP report of the filing. Distinct from the long-video topic 2026-11-19-kodak-digital: this Short turns on the $1 camera and the 15-cent film.

topics.title: Toys R Us Had 735 Stores in America. It Closed Every One

demand.title: Toys R Us Went Bankrupt. So Why Is It Still Here?

topics.hook: Toys R Us was where every birthday present came from, and in 2018 it closed every store it had in America.
topics.angle: The thing in your hand: the toy you unwrapped. September 2017: Toys R Us files for Chapter 11 with $5 billion in debt to repay. January 2018: it plans to close 180 stores. March 2018: it asks the court to liquidate all 735 U.S. stores, as many as 33,000 jobs (NBC News). It was about 10% of Mattel's and Hasbro's sales. Payoff: all 735. Global beat: the 100 U.K. stores closed too, while Canada, Central Europe and Asia were put up for sale.

topics.title: Sears Sold 70,000 Houses by Mail. Then It Couldn't Keep Its Stores

demand.title: How Sears was built

topics.hook: You could once order a whole house from the Sears catalog, and it came by train in 30,000 pieces.
topics.angle: The thing in your hand: the catalog. 1908 to 1940: Sears sells 70,000 to 75,000 mail-order homes in 447 styles, each kit 30,000 pieces by rail, one listed at $883 (CNBC). The store that could ship a house reached 4,000 stores in 2012; by May 2018 fewer than 900, and on 15 October 2018 it filed for Chapter 11 when a $134 million debt payment came due (PBS NewsHour / AP). Payoff: 4,000 to fewer than 900. Global beat: many of those kit houses still stand across the U.S.
topics.why_now: Rise Fall Repeat's 'How Sears was built' (90K on 19.9K, 4.5x) is one of its few Shorts to beat its channel; a catalog house is a thing people still live in. New subject for the channel.
